newsitem.title: DUBAI: SOCCER-SAUDIS REACH QUARTER-FINALS, IRAN REVIVE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAUDIS REACH QUARTER-FINALS, IRAN REVIVE HOPES.

text.p: Saudi Arabia became the first team to qualify for the quarter-finals of the Asian Cup with a 1-0 victory over Iraq in a group B match on Sunday.
Triple champions Iran kept their hopes of qualifying for the knockout stage alive with a 3-1 win over Thailand in the second group B match.
Thailand's second consecutive defeat means they are all but out of the 12-nation championship.
Saudi Arabia, champions in 1984 and 1988 and beaten finalists in 1992, justified their ranking as one of three favourites for the title with a good performance against a strong Iraqi team.
They now top group B with six points from two wins out of two games. Iran and Iraq have three points each and Thailand are without any.
The top two teams from the three groups qualify for the knockout stage, with the best two teams in third place also going through.
Saudi Arabia -- who crushed Thailand 6-0 -- will meet Iran, and Iraq play Thailand, in the final group B matches on Wednesday.
Striker Fahad Mahalel won the match for Saudi Arabia against Iraq in the 26th minute with his third goal of the tournament.
He controlled a pass from Khaled Al Temawi, slipped his marker and fired a 20-metre left-foot shot that beat Iraqi goalkeeper Emad Hassan.
The Iraqis hit the woodwork eight minutes later and had much of the play in the second half but found Saudi keeper Mohammed al-Daeyea -- one of the Saudi stars in the 1994 World Cup -- in fine form.
Iraq's veteran striker Laith Shihaib should have equalised in injury time but he delayed his shot with the goal at his mercy to allow the Saudi defenders to clear the danger.

Saudi Arabia's Portuguese coach Eduardo Vingada said: "The level of this match was better than many games during Euro 96. He said his team could still improve and was optimistic about their chances in the competition.
Iran striker Ali Daei repeatedly toyed with the Thai defenders in a match dominated by an Iranian side showing four changes from the team who lost to Iraq 2-1 on Thursday.

Defender Naeim Sadavi opened the scoring for Iran in the 37th minute with a spectacular low drive from outside the penalty area. Mehrdad Minavand got the second after 54 minutes with another spectacular shot from outside the box, this time in the top corner.
Daei's hard work was repaid with a goal in the 70th minute after fine control on the edge of the box.
Forward Kiatisk Senamuang scored a consolation goal for Thailand with 10 minutes to go.
Favourites Japan play Uzbekistan and China face Syria in group C matches on Monday. Japan beat Syria 2-1 and Uzbekistan overcame China 2-0 in their opening matches.
